description: Provenance ledger of the driving docs (00, 06-08, 10-13): one row per quantitative claim with the value as measured, the research-workspace experiment ID or bundled file that holds it, and the scope it was measured on. status 'supported' means the docs' figure equals the value in the row.

claims.claim: Object-list excursions ramp up over about 1 s
claims.source: research workspace SCR-417 (excursion cause): ensemble onset / end shapes
claims.note: Ensemble of 25 events; the onset ramps over about 1 s.

claims.claim: Object-list speed error against the ACC target: RMS about 0.8 m/s at code 15 and 1.2 m/s at code 30 (0.04-0.06 m/s per count)
claims.note: Measured RMS at codes 14.8 / 28.0 / 34.4; the K = 0.045 m/s per count model gives 1.35 at code 30.

claims.claim: On a highway about 2 slots hold objects on average (p95 4, up to 7)
claims.note: Drive C (highway); mean over non-empty records, 1.49 for settled tracks (age >= 60).

claims.claim: Roughness against vision only: +0.005 m/s2 RMS in steady following, +0.032 around radar / vision disagreements (20 % of the time)
claims.source: research workspace SCR-119; bundled jitter_problem_figures.json, jitter_source_and_interface_limit.json
claims.note: 20 held-out routes, `raw` object-list radar plus vision.

claims.claim: About 70 % of the extra roughness energy comes from the radar / vision disagreement windows
claims.note: Share 0.693 of the extra roughness, 20 held-out routes.

claims.claim: aRel lags vRel by about 0.5 s
claims.note: Correlation 0.22 with a broad peak over 0.3-0.9 s.

claims.claim: 17.5 % of radard ticks repeat the previous vRel; this adds about 1 % to aLeadK roughness
claims.note: aLeadK roughness 0.263 (held vRel) against 0.260 (fresh vRel), +1.2 %.

claims.claim: StarPilot drives: 2 drives (the earlier tuned profile)
claims.note: Openpilot longitudinal ran 8.0 and 9.7 min (17.7 min) in drives of 25 and 20 min.

claims.claim: sunnypilot drives with the earlier tuned profile: 2 drives
claims.note: Routes 3 and 4 of the series ran with the ARS510 active (flags 5465).

claims.claim: StarPilot's planner extrapolates lead acceleration unchanged above 35 mph (blend 20-35 mph)
Cost of the object-list decode: about 6-14 us per 10 ms call on a desktop CPU
claims.note: Measured on samples holding the bus-1 radar and 0xB4 frames.

claims.claim: check_integration.py passes 21-22 checks (current openpilot, the pinned replay base, sunnypilot v2026.002.002)
claims.note: Sunnypilot counts measured on the v2026.002.002 builds of 2026-09-28 / 30.

claims.claim: Range fusion (`fused`) cuts 1.5 s range walks by about a third
claims.note: Median ratio 0.68 (0.67 at 5-40 and 40-80 m, 0.78 at 80-160 m), computed on camera_pairs.parquet with the object list's own vRel.

claims.claim: `fused` aLeadK peaks in cross-correlation at a median 0 ticks against the tuned profile's (0 on 14 of 15 routes, 1 tick on one)
`raw` saturation guard: held-out hard ticks 117 to 93
23 owner road-drive bookmarks: `fused` 2.3 and 2.4 give the same minimum request on 19, within 0.03 m/s2 on the other 4
claims.note: Bookmarks: owner drive 1 11, drive 6 6, drive 5 5, drive 2 1. The extra-braking and missed-braking seconds are identical on all 23.

claims.claim: Road mild requests, `fused` 2.3 against 2.4: 7 each on the owner drives, 8 each with the second car
claims.note: Episode lists are identical: owner drives 1, 3, 4, 5 one each and drive 6 three (7), plus one on the second car (8).

claims.claim: Kalman bench: every cycle of 8 drive groups, tuned on 3 groups and scored on held-out / fresh / owner drives
Retuned `fused` constants (sigma per count 0.033, ACC sigma 0.3, lead acceleration 1.0 / 2.0) on 8 fresh drives: only lead acceleration 2.0 passes every gate, and it scores the same as 1.5
claims.value: sweep sigma per count 0.033, ACC sigma 0.3, lead acceleration 1.0 / 2.0 on 8 fresh drives
claims.note: The current constants sit at a flat optimum.

claims.claim: Colored-noise filter: 14 % and 16 % fewer false closings on held-out and fresh drives, equal on owner drives
claims.note: Bench false-closing shares in percent, `fused` then colored, then the relative change.

claims.claim: Colored-noise filter against `fused` on the further drives: 30 against 2 hard ticks
Publishing at age 40 raises further-drive hard ticks from 1 to 9
claims.note: Baseline is 2.3 (CL_P15S).

claims.claim: Publishing at age 80 raises missed braking against the hindsight-lead oracle from 3.3 to 3.7 s on 27 drives (measured on 2.3)
claims.note: A80 is built on 2.3's configuration (3.3 s), so the like-for-like change is 3.3 to 3.7 s.

claims.claim: Toyota ACC keeps a departing car until its centre is a median 1.64 m off-axis (middle half 0.67-2.16 m; 22 departures)
The release comes when the car's centre is a median 0.29 m inside the radar's lane line (21 departures; middle half -1.26 to +0.42 m)
On two matched cut-ins on the fresh drives (n = 2), openpilot's model moved to the new lead first (1.5 s and >= 6 s earlier)
claims.note: Three cut-in-like ACC switches in 1.9 h of fresh drives (routes 08 / 09 / 0a); two matched to a model lead change.

claims.claim: 0x235 byte 2 against a smoothed lead acceleration from the object-list speed: correlation 0.64 against 0.56 for radard's aLeadK, RMS 0.69 against 0.80 m/s2, wobble 0.13 against 0.15
claims.note: At the ACC unit of 0.125 m/s per code.

claims.claim: The upstream single file equals `fused` point for point on the bundled samples; on 2.4.1 also on two full road drives (200,209 points, 0 differences)
claims.source: research workspace SCR-476; bundled fused_filter.json (upstream_equality_2_4_1); tests/test_upstream_candidate.py
claims.note: tests/test_upstream_candidate.py covers each release on the bundled samples.

claims.claim: Ford radar_interface: 272 lines, 184 of them code
claims.note: The comparison table's rows are all counted at opendbc 6123dde9.

claims.claim: Tesla radar_interface: 66 code lines
claims.note: Toyota 70, Honda 60, Hyundai 55, Rivian 54, Chrysler 56, GM 71 at opendbc 6123dde9; opendbc 4134c0d has Tesla 62, Toyota 69.

claims.claim: 0x680 idle while driving: longest 1.0 s in 7.8 h of normal driving
claims.note: 7.25 h owner + 0.55 h held-out moving hours; the held-out longest idle is 0.5 s.

claims.claim: Driver-brake windows around the brake press: anticipation [-3, +0.5] s, first request [-3, +2] s, missed hard slowdown [-3, +1] s
claims.note: Table rows reading 'within 3 s before' (docs 08, 11) and profiles_vs_vision.json use the same windows.

claims.claim: 0x4FF is sent at about 0.8 Hz
claims.note: 46 frames per 60 s segment (0.77 Hz); the census prints 0.8.

claims.claim: 0x411 appears in 752 owner segments; 27 of them start with 40 20 ...
claims.note: The 27 start-up segments are part of the 752 (they also carry 00 20).

claims.claim: 0x366 coverage: owner drive O2 (13 segments, 3,748 frames) and O3 (4 segments, 1,200 frames)
